long_biography.plain_text:
Kevin Taylor worked with Phil Pringle at Birse and Fitzpatrick before they founded McLaren Construction in 2001. Taylor became chairman and retained decisive ownership as the contractor expanded through repeat customers and a widening range of building sectors. The business grew from its Essex base into commercial, residential, industrial, logistics, leisure, data-centre and public-sector work across Britain and the Middle East.

Taylor remains chairman as operational leadership has widened beneath him. McLaren's turnover passed the billion-pound threshold while he retained more than three quarters of its shares and voting rights. As chairman, he selects senior leaders, backs new regional divisions and sets the group's direction while a separate chief executive manages construction operations.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative input links person 2481 to Thumper during 2014–2020 and to Mousea of the Sea from January 2026. A property-industry source independently places Kevin Taylor from the McLaren group aboard his boat Thumper in Cannes during that period, resolving the collision-prone name. Public Mousea of the Sea sources confirm the exact yacht but keep ownership behind a subscription, so the new current relationship remains anchored in the immutable input rather than an independently visible beneficial-owner chain.

McLaren Construction Group is unrelated to McLaren Automotive and the Formula One team. A different British Kevin Taylor worked as a Formula One design engineer; none of that engineer's roles, education or sporting history is transferred here. The exact full name, construction shareholding, Phil Pringle relationship and Thumper bridge identify the construction founder.

A Luxembourg filing placed Taylor in Monte Carlo in 2012, and one current Companies House officer record for KRT Trading lists Monaco. The identity-verified McLaren controlling-person record lists the United Kingdom, while older duplicate officer records also show France. Because public filings conflict and may describe different dates or capacities, no main or secondary residence country is proposed.

Forbes-first exact-name searches found no dedicated individual profile. Coverage of McLaren Automotive, McLaren Racing and similarly named executives was excluded rather than treated as Taylor's profile.

Industry reporting establishes earlier employment at Birse and Fitzpatrick before Taylor co-founded McLaren Construction, and no reviewed source identifies an inherited company or family-capital platform. Initial financing and any private family resources are undisclosed, so Self-made — independent start remains below very-high confidence.

Companies House records at least 75% of shares and voting rights plus director-appointment power, but not a precise economic percentage or current private-company valuation. The dossier therefore describes controlling ownership without estimating Taylor's net worth or the value of his stake.
Strong exact-person corporate records establish British nationality only. Monaco and France residence history does not establish citizenship, so secondary nationality remains blank.

McLaren's exact-person official leadership page is proposed as the Company Website. Focused searches did not verify personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal-website profiles above threshold; namesake accounts and company social pages were not substituted.

The biographies omit both yachts, private-company valuation, point-in-time forecasts, project values, private residence details and unrelated namesake records. No live or compiled change is authorised.
